f.title: Run non-interventional Phase IV safety studies under the SFDA GVP
f.statement: For non-interventional Phase IV trials that aim to gather safety information on registered products, and for registry observational studies, the applicant should adhere to the Good Pharmacovigilance Practices (GVP) guideline.
f.applicability: Non-interventional Phase IV safety studies and registry observational studies on registered products
f.exceptions: Surveys and questionnaires (e.g. satisfaction, awareness) are exempt from SCTR registration.
f.processes: Epidemiology / safety studies; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.quote: Non-interventional phase IV trials which aim to gather safety information on registered products or registry observational studies, the applicant should adhere to the Good Pharmacovigilance Practices Guideline (GVP).
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: should = Recommended.

f.title: Consult the Drug Safety and Risk Management Department on risk minimisation (RIMS) studies
f.statement: Risk minimisation studies and studies of the effectiveness of implemented risk minimisation measures (RIMS) must be consulted with the SFDA Drug Safety and Risk Management Department.
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Epidemiology / safety studies

rows.quote: Risk minimization studies and Effectiveness of Implemented Risk Minimization Measures studies (RIMS) must be consulted by the Drug Safety and Risk Management Department at
rows.review_note: Review: quote stops before the department e-mail address. Double-check: "must be consulted by" read as must be consulted with the department.

f.title: Implement urgent safety amendments immediately and notify SFDA and the IRB at once
f.statement: Upon exposure of any trial participant to a hazard or harm, the applicant is authorised to implement the necessary amendment immediately; concurrently the applicant must provide immediate formal notification, including the IRB notification, to SFDA by email.
f.clause: 7. Clinical trials in phase I, II, III - C. Clinical trials amendments

rows.quote: Upon the exposure of any trial participant to a hazard or harm, the applicant is authorized to implement the necessary amendment immediately. Concurrently, the applicant must provide immediate formal notification, including the IRB notification,
rows.location: 7. Clinical trials in phase I, II, III - C. Clinical trials amendments
rows.review_note: Review: quote stops before the e-mail address. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Submit annual progress reports (Form No. 1) with site delegation logs and GCP training proof
f.statement: The applicant must submit a progress report annually for ongoing trials using the Progress Report (Form No. 1), one year after approval; if the trial lasts less than one year, after half the study duration. The delegation log for each site and proof of adequate GCP training of the research team must also be submitted. Form No. 1 includes a safety section on SUSARs and DSUR status.
f.clause: 7. Clinical trials in phase I, II, III - B

rows.deadline: Annually, first one year after approval (after half the study duration for trials under one year)
rows.quote: This report must be submitted after obtaining the approval by one year. However, in case the trial duration is less than one year, the applicant must submit the progress report after half the study duration has passed.
rows.location: 7. Clinical trials in phase I, II, III - B
rows.review_note: Review: kept because Form No. 1 carries the SUSAR/DSUR safety section. Double-check: deadline_rule as 12 months from approval for the first report; recurring annual thereafter.

f.title: Report SUSARs (local and global) on Form No. 2 within 15 days, with follow-up
f.statement: It is mandatory to inform SFDA immediately about any suspected unexpected serious adverse reaction (SUSAR), for both local and global cases of trials ongoing in Saudi Arabia, on Form No. 2 as soon as possible and no later than 15 days, followed by the follow-up report.
f.applicability: Local and global SUSARs of trials ongoing in Saudi Arabia

rows.deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 15 days, followed by follow-up report
rows.quote: It is mandatory to inform the SFDA immediately about any suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions (SUSAR) for both local and global cases of ongoing trials in Saudi Arabia on “Form No. 2” as soon as possible, no later than 15 days followed by the follow-up report.
rows.review_note: Review: no deadline_rule: the source gives no clock start (ICH E2A day 0 is first knowledge by the sponsor). Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Report fatal or life-threatening SUSARs within 7 days
f.statement: If the SUSAR is fatal or life-threatening, SFDA must be informed as soon as possible and no later than seven days, in accordance with ICH E2A.

rows.deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 7 days
rows.quote: If the SUSAR is fatal or life threating, SFDA must be informed as soon as possible, no later than seven days in accordance with the ICH-E2A guideline,
rows.review_note: Review: no clock start in the source, so no deadline_rule. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Follow a fatal or life-threatening SUSAR with a follow-up report within 8 days
f.statement: The 7-day report of a fatal or life-threatening SUSAR must be followed by a follow-up report within 8 days.

rows.deadline: Within 8 days after the initial report
rows.quote: with a follow-up report succeeding it within 8 days.
rows.review_note: Review: split from the 7-day row; no clock wording beyond "succeeding it", so no deadline_rule. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Send SUSARs via the National Pharmacovigilance Center with the SCTR number and "SUSAR Case" subject
f.statement: SUSARs should be reported through the National Pharmacovigilance Center by email; the SCTR number must be provided and the email must be titled "SUSAR Case".

rows.quote: It is necessary to provide the SCTR number and the e-mail must be titled as “SUSAR Case.”
rows.review_note: Review: e-mail address omitted (checker rule). Double-check: channel itself is "should"; SCTR number and subject line are "necessary/must".

f.title: Send SUSARs in XML format plus a CIOMS form
f.statement: The applicant must send SUSARs in XML format in addition to completing the CIOMS form; when the report is submitted by the researcher, sending it on the attached Form 2 is adequate.
f.exceptions: Researcher-submitted reports may use Form 2 alone.

rows.quote: The applicant must send SUSARs in (XML) format in addition to complete the Council for International Organizations of Medical Sciences (CIOMS) Form. It is adequate to send the report to the attached form 2, when submitted by the researcher.

f.title: Report local trial SUSARs/AEs to the Clinical Trials Department
f.statement: Clinical trial related local SUSARs/adverse events are expected for all clinical trials registered in the SCTR platform and approved by SFDA for conduct in Saudi Arabia, and should be reported to the Clinical Trials Department by email.
f.applicability: Trials registered in the SCTR and approved by SFDA

rows.quote: Clinical trials related local SUSARs/Adverse Events are anticipated for all clinical trials registered in the SCTR platform and only approved by the SFDA for conduction in Saudi, and should be reported to Clinical Trials Department via Email
rows.review_note: Review: quote stops before the e-mail address. Double-check: should = Recommended.

f.title: Report per-protocol IP SUSARs only; foreign SUSARs may be sent as periodic line listings
f.statement: Reported SUSARs are for investigational products (pre- and post-authorisation) per protocol only. Periodic line listings are acceptable for foreign SUSARs.

rows.quote: Reported SUSARs for investigational products (pre and post authorization) per protocol only. Periodic line listing is acceptable for foreign SUSARs.
rows.review_note: Review: line-listing option recorded as Permitted; scope limitation in statement. Double-check: tension with 11.A (global cases on Form 2) left as in source.

f.title: Submit the DSUR annually with the SCTR number
f.statement: The applicant must submit the development safety update report (DSUR) annually to SFDA with the SCTR number (the source cites ICH E2A). If the full DSUR is not available, an executive summary shall be submitted with justification.

rows.quote: The applicant must annually submit the development safety update report (DSUR) in accordance with the ICH-E2A guideline to the Authority with the SCTR number. If the full DSUR is not available, an executive summary shall be submitted with justification.
rows.review_note: Review: source cites ICH E2A for the DSUR (ICH E2F is the DSUR guideline); kept as written. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Progress report: confirm SUSARs were notified within 7/15 days and state DSUR status
f.statement: In the progress report (Form No. 1), the applicant must state whether there have been SUSARs in the trial in Saudi Arabia, whether they were notified to SFDA within 7 or 15 days (and, if not, arrange notification urgently and give reasons for the late notification), whether the DSUR has been submitted and when the next DSUR is due.
f.clause: Annex - Form No. 1 Progress Report, 5. Safety reports
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Quality system & CAPA

rows.quote: Have these SUSARs been notified to SFDA within 7 or 15 days in accordance with SFDA Regulations and Requirements for Conducting Clinical Trials on Drugs? Yes / No If no, please arrange urgently and give reasons for late notification.
rows.location: Annex - Form No. 1 Progress Report, 5. Safety reports
rows.review_note: Review: form questions read as required content. Double-check: level could be argued Recommended.

f.title: Investigator commits to report adverse experiences to the sponsor
f.statement: In the Statement of Investigator (Form No. 4), the investigator agrees to report to the sponsor adverse experiences that occur in the course of the investigation in accordance with the regulatory requirements, having read the investigator's brochure including potential risks and side effects.
f.clause: Annex - Form No. 4 Statement of Investigator, Commitments
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Safety intake & collection

rows.quote: I agree to report to the sponsor adverse experiences that occur in the course of the investigation(s) in accordance with the regulatory requirement.
rows.location: Annex - Form No. 4 Statement of Investigator, Commitments
rows.review_note: Review: signed commitment, treated as binding. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Investigator maintains adequate and accurate records per ICH E6 and makes them available
f.statement: The investigator agrees to maintain adequate and accurate records in accordance with ICH GCP E6 and to make them available for inspection in accordance with GCP E6.
f.clause: Annex - Form No. 4 Statement of Investigator, Commitments
f.processes: Data integrity & records; Audit & inspection readiness

rows.quote: I agree to maintain adequate and accurate records in accordance with GCP E6 and to make those records available for inspection in accordance with GCP E6.
rows.location: Annex - Form No. 4 Statement of Investigator, Commitments

f.title: Investigator promptly reports unanticipated risks to the IRB
f.statement: The investigator agrees to promptly report to the IRB all changes in the research activity and all unanticipated problems involving risks to human subjects or others, and not to make changes without IRB approval except to eliminate apparent immediate hazards.
f.clause: Annex - Form No. 4 Statement of Investigator, Commitments

rows.quote: I also agree to promptly report to the IRB all changes in the research activity and all unanticipated problems involving risks to human subjects or others.
rows.location: Annex - Form No. 4 Statement of Investigator, Commitments

f.title: Expanded-access physician reports results including adverse drug reactions
f.statement: In the request form for access to a non-marketed drug, the physician/principal investigator agrees to provide the progress report and a report on the results of use of the drug, including information on adverse drug reactions, and, on request, to account for quantities of the drug received.
f.clause: Annex - Post-Trial Access Program Clearance Request form, Section F: Applicant attestation
f.applicability: Access to non-marketed drugs for a patient (post-trial access / compassionate use)

rows.quote: I, the physician/principal investigator, agree to provide the progress report and a report on the results of the use of the drug including information on adverse drug reactions and, on request, to account for quantities of the drug received.
rows.location: Annex - Post-Trial Access Program Clearance Request form, Section F: Applicant attestation
rows.review_note: Review: attestation treated as binding. Double-check: form identity inferred from its position after the PTAP form heading.
